verdict.rationale: Name.com documents a dedicated sandbox (testing) environment. It mirrors production request/response shapes and lets users run automated integration tests without affecting real domains or incurring charges. Separate development and production API tokens back this up. This is true environment isolation, not a dry-run flag. Missing for 10: detailed sandbox documentation (endpoint hosts, test-data behavior, limitations versus production) and independent or hands-on corroboration that the sandbox works as described.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: provides a **sandbox (testing) environment** that mirrors production request/response shapes, so you can build and run automated integration tests without affecting real domains or incurring real charges
Go to Account Settings → Security → API Tokens and issue both development and production tokens
